author: reek
body: The "thread" field is ignored here; threaded discussion lives in Discussion, not plain Annotation. Unknown kinds map to Discovery (the most permissive bucket).

author: reek
body: parse-sidecar takes the chapter name (for the AnnotationTarget) and the raw JSON text. Returns a list of Annotation records; invalid records are silently dropped (an annotation is dropped if its target or kind is missing -- since the system can do nothing useful with them -- and the rest still load). Returns None only if the JSON itself fails to parse.

author: reek
body: Discussion entries in the sidecar JSON have kind "discussion" and carry a "thread" id. They belong in the DiscussionStore, not the AnnotationStore -- Codex's discussion layer is a first-class peer of annotation, not a sub-kind. The reader routes them via discuss().

author: reek
body: fold-sidecar-entry handles one JSON object out of the sidecar array. Branches on the "kind" field; routes annotations to the store and discussions to the thread, dropping entries that lack the bare-minimum fields.

author: reek
body: load-sidecar is the convenience that takes a base AnnotationFact and a sidecar's chapter+text and returns the fact augmented with all parseable entries. A None from json-parse (JSON itself failed) yields the base fact unchanged. The "thread" id is read but the threading semantics are handled by Discussion (one thread per target).

author: reek
body: The full path is annotations/<quire>/<chapter>.json. The quire prefix depends on the source's quire and the caller knows that better than this chapter does, so the builder takes both explicitly.
